summary.text: Melissa Dicranian is the Republican candidate for Pennsylvania State Senate District 44 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Democrat Katie Muth.
A business owner who ran unsuccessfully for the Pennsylvania House in 2022 and 2024, she chairs a township historic architectural review board.

paragraphs.text: Melissa Dicranian was born in Maine and earned a bachelor's degree from the Wentworth Institute of Technology in 1993, according to Ballotpedia.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, her campaign biography said she grew up in a family of small business owners and worked for architectural firms as a designer, owner's representative and architectural representative.
It also said she chairs the Historic Architectural Review Board in Charlestown Township, serves as liaison to its planning and zoning body, and is a Pennsylvania Farm Bureau member.
Dicranian ran for Pennsylvania House District 167 in 2022 and lost the Republican primary to Gail Newman.
She won the Republican primary for the same seat on April 23, 2024, and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Kristine Howard, receiving 41.4 percent of the vote.
She advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for State Senate District 44 without opposition.
In the 2024 survey, Dicranian listed supporting economic growth, community safety and education as her priorities, including support for small businesses, pro-growth tax reform and school choice.
